## Motivation `DeepSeekV32Detector.parse_streaming_increment`, which the V4 and V4.1 detectors inherit, keeps a long-form invoke in `_buffer` until `` arrives. On every delta it runs `re.search(self.invoke_regex, current_text, re.DOTALL)` over the whole buffer, only to find that the invoke is still open and break out of the loop. The `(?P.*?)(?P(?:|$))` part lazily walks the entire held body each time. So each delta costs O(n) in the length of the call, and one long tool call costs O(n^2). We hit this in production serving of DeepSeek V4.1 with long agentic tool calls, where `write_file` / edit-style calls carry 20-30K tokens of code in one string parameter. On an older build, from before #39632, the same path also re-parsed and diffed the partial arguments on every delta. That capped delivery at about 1-2K tok/s per replica once a few such calls were in flight, and it backed up the tokenizer-manager output path. #39632 removed argument streaming, which cut the cost about 6x, but the re-scan is still quadratic. On current `main` (14ad64c4), a 30K-token call in 18-char deltas costs 3.5 s of CPU, and each delta near the end of the call costs about 1.2 ms. That works out to: - about 4K tok/s for one stream near the end of the call; - about 12.8K tok/s parse-only ceiling for six concurrent 20K-token calls, on one fast core. Profile on `main` (V4.1, 10K-token string parameter, 1,959 deltas): 0.389 s of the 0.406 s total (96%) is `re.Pattern.search`. Everything else is constant per delta. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/function_call/deepseekv32_detector.py`, +33 lines. Nothing else changes. - When the loop breaks on an open long-form invoke, record `(buffer, scan_from)` in `self._open_invoke`. `scan_from` is the start of the invoke body, or `len(buffer) - len(invoke_end_token) + 1` if that is later. - On the next delta, if `self._buffer` is still that exact object, search only from `scan_from` for `invoke_end_token`: - **No closer:** re-arm and return `StreamingParseResult()`. This is exactly what the full path returns for an open invoke, and the full path changes no state other than the buffer. - **Closer found:** fall through to the unchanged full path. That path runs the regex once, completes the call, and handles any following invokes. - Everything else runs the existing code as before. This covers the first chunk of each invoke, the completion chunk, self-closing invokes, `finish()`, a buffer replaced from outside (`_buffer` is not the recorded object), and a subclass that replaces `invoke_regex` or `invoke_end_token` after `__init__` (the fast path is never armed). Why this preserves behaviour: - **The open invoke stays the leftmost match.** An earlier start position fails only on header text that was already complete in the old buffer, because the header's `[^"]+` name ends at the first `"`, which lies at or before the open invoke's own header. Adding text cannot change that. - **A closer can only appear in new text.** The body ends at the first closer after the header, or at `$`. Any closer starting before `old_len - len(closer) + 1` would have been entirely inside the old buffer, and it was not there. - **Nothing else would change.** With a closer still missing, the original code returns `normal_text=""` and no calls, and it changes nothing except the buffer. `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_deepseek_dsml_long_streaming.py` (new, CPU), for V3.2, V4 and V4.1. Each transcript is a 3K-char code string parameter that contains `<`, `` / `

` / `a<3`):** 1,537 ns per delta on `main`, 1,590 ns with this PR, about +3% (~50 ns). That comes from one extra attribute swap and an `is` check per delta. What remains O(n) per delta is `self._buffer += new_text`, a C-level copy that the buffer contract already requires. +1, we ran into the same thing serving DeepSeek V4. Sometimes the model gets stuck repeating inside a string arg, e.g. a `Bash` `command` that keeps growing to a few hundred k chars until `max_tokens`. With the rescan on every delta, that one request blocks the event loop and every other request times out, health checks too. We made pretty much the same fix on our side and the hang went away.

One more thing, not blocking. `self._buffer += new_text` still copies the whole buffer on every delta (CPython's in-place concat doesn't kick in for attributes). It doesn't matter at the sizes in your table, but it adds up when the model loops. 4-char deltas into a string param:

| chars in the open invoke | this PR | also keep deltas out of `_buffer` until the closer |
|---|---|---|
| 120,000 | 0.28s | 0.13s |
| 480,000 | 5.31s | 0.52s |
| 1,920,000 | 98.15s | 2.05s |

Each delta is still well under 1ms, so it's not a hang, just more total CPU. The catch is `_buffer` falls behind while the invoke is open, so your per-delta `_buffer` check would need to change. Happy to send it as a small follow-up after this lands, if you want.

@@ -99,6 +99,11 @@ def __init__(self):
             rf"|>(?P<body>.*?)(?P<end>(?:</{invoke}>|$)))"
         )
         self.current_tool_id = -1
+        # Streaming fast path for a long-form invoke whose closer has not
+        # arrived yet; see parse_streaming_increment. It is only armed while
+        # invoke_regex / invoke_end_token are still the ones built here.
+        self._open_invoke_tokens = (self.invoke_regex, self.invoke_end_token)
+        self._open_invoke = None
 
     def has_tool_call(self, text: str) -> bool:
         """Check if the text contains a deepseek v32 format tool call."""
@@ -256,9 +261,23 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
         Streaming incremental parsing tool calls for DeepSeekV32 format.
         Supports multiple consecutive invoke blocks.
         """
+        open_invoke, self._open_invoke = self._open_invoke, None
+        held_text = self._buffer
         self._buffer += new_text
         current_text = self._buffer
 
+        # While a long-form invoke is open, the buffer holds all of it and
+        # nothing is emitted until its closer arrives. Re-matching invoke_regex
+        # over the held body on every delta is quadratic in the length of the
+        # call. The open invoke stays the leftmost match (its header is
+        # complete), and a closer starting before scan_from was already ruled
+        # out, so only the text that just arrived needs to be searched.
+        if open_invoke is not None and open_invoke[0] is held_text:
+            scan_from = open_invoke[1]
+            if current_text.find(self.invoke_end_token, scan_from) == -1:
+                self._arm_open_invoke(current_text, scan_from)
+                return StreamingParseResult()
+
         # Check if buffer contains any DSML markers or ends with potential tag prefix
         # This handles partial/streaming DSML content
         bar = self.dsml_token[0]
@@ -308,6 +327,8 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
                     invoke_match
                 )
                 if not is_tool_end:
+                    if invoke_match.group("body") is not None:
+                        self._arm_open_invoke(current_text, invoke_match.start("body"))
                     break
 
                 # Initialize state on the first complete invoke, malformed or
@@ -371,7 +392,19 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
                 preamble = self._text_before_dsml(current_text)
             return StreamingParseResult(normal_text=preamble, calls=all_calls)
 
+    def _arm_open_invoke(self, text: str, scan_from: int) -> None:
+        """Record that `text` (the buffer) ends inside an open long-form invoke
+        and holds no closer at or after `scan_from`, which is at or after the
+        start of its body."""
+        if self._open_invoke_tokens != (self.invoke_regex, self.invoke_end_token):
+            return

+            max(scan_from, len(text) - len(self.invoke_end_token) + 1),

+"""Long DSML tool calls streamed in small deltas (DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1).
+
+The streaming detector holds an open invoke in its buffer until the closer
+arrives. These tests check that the open-invoke shortcut returns exactly what
+a full re-scan of the buffer returns, and that the work per delta does not grow
+with the length of the call.
+"""
+
+import json
+import re
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
+from sglang.srt.function_call.deepseekv4_detector import DeepSeekV4Detector
+from sglang.srt.function_call.deepseekv32_detector import DeepSeekV32Detector
+from sglang.srt.function_call.deepseekv41_detector import DeepSeekV41Detector
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+DETECTORS = [DeepSeekV32Detector, DeepSeekV4Detector, DeepSeekV41Detector]
+CHUNK_SIZES = [1, 3, 7, 18]
+
+
+def _tools():
+    return [
+        Tool(
+            type="function",
+            function=Function(
+                name=name,
+                parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}},
+            ),
+        )
+        for name in ("write_file", "lookup", "list_files")
+    ]
+
+
+def _code(detector, n_chars):
+    """Code-like text with `<`, `</` and partial DSML closers, none complete."""
+    pieces = [
+        "def f(x):\n",
+        "    return x < 3 and y </ 2\n",
+        '    s = "<div>\\n"\n',
+        f"    # {detector.invoke_end_token[:-1]} is not a closer\n",
+        f"    # nor is <{detector.dsml_token}\n",
+        "    # 中文 é\n",
+    ]
+    out = []
+    while sum(map(len, out)) < n_chars:
+        out.extend(pieces)
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+def _transcript(detector_cls, n_chars):
+    d = detector_cls()
+    parameter = f"{d.dsml_token}{detector_cls.parameter_tag_name}"
+    code = _code(d, n_chars)
+    text = (
+        "Let me write the file.\n\n"
+        f"{d.bot_token}\n"
+        f'{d.invoke_start_token} name="write_file">\n'
+        f'<{parameter} name="path" string="true">src/app.py</{parameter}>\n'
+        f'<{parameter} name="content" string="true">{code}</{parameter}>\n'
+        f"{d.invoke_end_token}\n"
+        f'{d.invoke_start_token} name="lookup">\n'
+        + json.dumps({"query": code}, ensure_ascii=False)
+        + f"\n{d.invoke_end_token}\n"
+        f'{d.invoke_start_token} name="list_files"/>\n'
+        f"{d.eot_token}"
+    )
+    expected = [
+        ("write_file", {"path": "src/app.py", "content": code}),
+        ("lookup", {"query": code}),
+        ("list_files", {}),
+    ]
+    if d.strip_string_param_value:
+        expected[0] = ("write_file", {"path": "src/app.py", "content": code.strip()})
+    return text, expected
+
+
+def _split(text, size):
+    return [text[i : i + size] for i in range(0, len(text), size)]
+
+
+def _results(results):
+    return [
+        (r.normal_text, [(c.tool_index, c.name, c.parameters) for c in r.calls])
+        for r in results
+    ]
+
+
+class TestDeepSeekDsmlLongStreaming(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_incremental_matches_full_rescan(self):
+        """Per delta, the results equal those of a detector that re-scans the
+        whole buffer every time (open-invoke shortcut cleared before each delta)."""
+        tools = _tools()
+        for detector_cls in DETECTORS:
+            text, expected = _transcript(detector_cls, 3000)
+            for size in CHUNK_SIZES:
+                with self.subTest(detector=detector_cls.__name__, chunk_size=size):
+                    incremental, rescan = detector_cls(), detector_cls()
+                    got, want = [], []
+                    for chunk in _split(text, size):
+                        got.append(incremental.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, tools))
+                        rescan._open_invoke = None
+                        want.append(rescan.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, tools))
+                        self.assertEqual(incremental._buffer, rescan._buffer)
+                    self.assertEqual(_results(got), _results(want))
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        incremental.finish(tools).model_dump(),
+                        rescan.finish(tools).model_dump(),
+                    )
+
+                    normal = "".join(r.normal_text for r in got)
+                    calls = [c for r in got for c in r.calls]
+                    self.assertEqual(normal, "Let me write the file.")
+                    self.assertEqual([c.tool_index for c in calls], [0, 1, 2])
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        [(c.name, json.loads(c.parameters)) for c in calls], expected
+                    )
+
+    def test_open_invoke_is_not_rescanned_per_delta(self):
+        """Characters handed to re.search stay linear in the length of the call
+        (a full re-scan per delta would be quadratic)."""
+        tools = _tools()
+        real_search = re.search
+        for detector_cls in DETECTORS:
+            text, expected = _transcript(detector_cls, 60_000)
+            scanned = [0]
+
+            def counting_search(pattern, string, flags=0):
+                scanned[0] += len(string)
+                return real_search(pattern, string, flags)
+
+            with self.subTest(detector=detector_cls.__name__):
+                detector = detector_cls()
+                calls = []
+                with patch.object(re, "search", counting_search):
+                    for chunk in _split(text, 18):
+                        calls.extend(
+                            detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, tools).calls
+                        )
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    [(c.name, json.loads(c.parameters)) for c in calls], expected
+                )
+                self.assertLess(scanned[0], 4 * len(text))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
